title: Use Matrices as Transformations
core_invariant: A matrix is a transformation with named input and output axes. Composition order is executable architecture, not typography. Single vectors are columns y = A x; row-major batches use X @ A.T. Predict landmark movement before multiplying. Diagnose wrong order and wrong orientation from counterexamples, not from a plausible plot.

stages.title: Frame matrices as visual transformations
stages.instructions: Read the M16 invariant: see a transformation before formalizing matrix algebra. Convention: a single vector is a column y = A x; a batch stores one sample per row and transforms as X @ A.T. Identify gate evidence: landmark predictions, scale/rotate/shear matrices, composition-order comparison, wrong-order and wrong-orientation diagnoses, a shape table, and a no-AI pipeline. Generic WP-137 chart, table, and metric blocks; no custom frontend.

stages.title: Trace y = A x versus the batch expression
stages.instructions: Read a transformation helper. Locate the single-vector product, the batch product, and any transpose. For each operand name the semantic axis (features in, features out, batch). Predict a landmark under a non-symmetric matrix before execution, and state what X @ A would mean under the mission convention.

validation_rubric.pass_criteria: Trace names axis roles and justifies any transpose from representation, not habit.

stages.title: Predict composition order, then execute
stages.instructions: Complete the experiment cycle on the generic runtime. (1) PREDICT the observable outcome before any numbers appear. (2) COMMIT the prediction so it cannot be edited. (3) EXECUTE / RUN the measurement. (4) OBSERVE structured WP-137 blocks. (5) SUBMIT / EXPLAIN any delta between prediction and observation. Compare shear-then-rotate with rotate-then-shear on landmark [1, 0]. Predict intermediate and final coordinates. Emit a WP-137 metric of both results and a table of application order versus written matrix order. Keep the useful geometry identical while changing only composition.

validation_rubric.pass_criteria: Prediction is sealed before execute; the two orders disagree on a documented landmark.

stages.title: Diagnose wrong order and wrong batch orientation
stages.instructions: Two seeded faults, each with one root cause. Fault A composes rotation and shear in reverse application order; run the smallest one-vector counterexample and identify the first diverging intermediate. Fault B computes X @ A for square A, which runs and preserves (n, 2) but applies A.T @ x per row. Use a non-symmetric matrix and one landmark. Repair A by restoring application order; repair B as X @ A.T. A plausible plot is a symptom, not verification.

validation_rubric.pass_criteria: Each fault has a counterexample, first divergence, smallest repair, and restated invariant.

stages.title: Fresh batch pipeline without assistance
stages.instructions: Without AI-generated code, apply scale (1.5, 0.5), horizontal shear -0.4, then 30° rotation to a fresh (n, 2) polygon stored one point per row. Predict a landmark, write the three elementary matrices and the composite with application order, justify any transpose, include a shape table, assert composite-batch equals the three-step batch, show one reversed order differs, and connect the pattern to a dense ML layer X @ W + b.

validation_rubric.pass_criteria: Fresh no-AI pipeline with predictions, shapes, order counterexample, and ML-layer mapping.

stages.title: Record the batch-orientation contract
stages.instructions: Complete an ADR for the V04 matrix convention: column-vector y = A x versus row-batch X @ A.T. Reject storing samples as columns without an explicit conversion. State migration cost and a condition that would justify revisiting.

validation_rubric.pass_criteria: ADR chooses one convention, rejects the alternative with a concrete orientation failure, and names a revisit trigger.

stages.title: Connect matrix instruments to V04
stages.instructions: Explain how M16 supplies V04's transformation and batch-shape instruments: matrices as functions, predicted landmark movement, composition as architecture, named batch/feature/output axes, justified transposes, and sample-wise equivalence. With row-major X (batch, in_features) and W (in_features, out_features), a dense layer is X @ W + b, which agrees with A = W.T.

stages.title: Evaluate transformation evidence
stages.instructions: Evaluate orientation, experiment, controlled-failure, transfer, and ADR evidence. Issue PASSED or a targeted repair plan. Do not award completion from a plot that merely looks reasonable.
